claim_judgments.rationale: No supported contrast: the draft's stated applicability matches the source rule under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(1). The prohibition correctly binds the pilot from taking off without the required passenger briefing, preserving the exceptions for free balloons with baskets/gondolas and airships certificated prior to November 2, 1987, as well as the overarching Administrator authorization caveat.

No supported contrast: the draft's stated applicability matches the source rule under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(2). It accurately states that no pilot may cause a U.S.-registered civil aircraft to move on the surface, take off, or land without ensuring passengers are notified to fasten safety belts and shoulder harnesses if installed, subject to the standard balloon/airship exclusions and Administrator authorization.

No supported contrast: the draft matches the source requirement under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3) governing occupants during surface movement, takeoff, and landing on U.S.-registered civil aircraft. Governing exceptions (balloon, airship, paragraph (a)(3) exceptions, and Administrator authorization) are faithfully preserved.
No supported contrast: the draft matches the source exemption under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3) for personnel pushing off or mooring seaplanes or float-equipped rotorcraft at a dock during surface movement.

No supported contrast: the draft matches the permission in 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(i). It accurately describes the conditions under which a child under age two may be held by an adult occupying an approved seat or berth without restraining devices.
No supported contrast: the draft accurately reflects the permission in 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(ii) allowing persons on board for sport parachuting to use the aircraft floor as a seat.

No supported contrast: the draft accurately conveys the permission in 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii) to occupy an approved child restraint system, retaining the conditions concerning accompanying adult attendants and qualifying label requirements.

No supported contrast: the draft accurately specifies the required label wording for child restraint systems manufactured between January 1, 1981, and February 25, 1985, under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(1).

No supported contrast: the draft accurately captures the two-label requirement and specific text/red lettering requirements for seats manufactured on or after February 26, 1985, under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(2).

No supported contrast: the draft comprehensively captures the three alternative labeling/marking criteria under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(3) for seats not qualifying under (B)(1) or (B)(2), correctly structuring them with choice_text and alternative_quotes across U0009, U0010, and U0011.

No supported contrast: the draft faithfully preserves the specific grandfathering permission for the AmSafe CARES Part No. 4082 child restraint device bearing FAA approval under 14 CFR 21.305(d) (2010 ed.).

No supported contrast: the draft faithfully represents the prohibition and unapproved status in 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(4) for booster-type, vest- and harness-type, and lap-held child restraints, except as provided in paragraphs (B)(3)(iii) and (iv).

No supported contrast: the draft accurately reflects the operator duty under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(1) requiring the restraint system to be properly secured to an approved forward-facing seat or berth.

No supported contrast: the draft accurately reflects the operator compliance requirement under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(2) ensuring the child is properly secured and does not exceed the weight limit.
No supported contrast: the draft accurately reflects the operator compliance duty under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(3) requiring that the restraint system bears the appropriate label(s).
No supported contrast: the draft matches the general carveout in 14 CFR 91.107(b) stating that the section does not apply to operations under part 121, 125, or 135 unless otherwise stated.
No supported contrast: the draft matches the exemption in 14 CFR 91.107(b) providing that paragraph (a)(3) does not apply to persons subject to section 91.105.
